description: The reference rewritten from scratch: four renamed capabilities (scene-runtime, viewer-controls, presentation-authoring, release-checks), merged and split requirements, new wording throughout, and swapped mechanisms for every acceptable alternative whose mechanism can change. Every requirement is kept.

swapped_alternatives.mechanism: Sections come from a per-presentation chapter list naming each chapter's first step id, not a per-step section/era label.
A required reader `body` plus an optional speaker `headline` that falls back to the body's first sentence, instead of two mandatory texts.
Newcomers are revealed one after another on a separate reveal layer that never alters continuing entities' paths, instead of waiting for persisting entities to settle.
Dropped entities dissolve and are removed from the document before newcomers are revealed.
One scene instance is mounted per presentation and fed each step's state; there are no scene groups.
Continuing entities are matched by key and animated with FLIP measurement rather than layout projection.
A `classNames` slot map passed to `<Presentation>` instead of stable class/data DOM hooks.
A `Positioned` primitive with explicit per-step coordinates and `useEntity(id)` for custom elements, instead of raw motion elements with layout ids.
Present mode shows a lower-third headline strip with a step counter; the body goes to a separate presenter-notes window.
Browse mode uses a side panel with clickable progress segments and a chapter outline that collapses into a menu below 720px.
ArrowRight/ArrowDown/Space forward and ArrowLeft/ArrowUp/Shift+Space back, instead of PageDown/PageUp.
`aria-current="step"`, a polite live-region announcement, and a `current` slot class.
Clamped ends with an edge nudge at the start and an "End" marker at the finish.
An SVG `viewBox` with `preserveAspectRatio` scales the fixed coordinate space, instead of a computed transform.
The fit is measured from the active mode's stage region with a ResizeObserver, instead of fixed per-mode geometry constants.
The look is chosen from style directions derived from the host's stylesheets (or three neutral directions).
A "build now" checkpoint after each batch of answers drafts undescribed steps as `TODO` placeholders.
A hand-edited `src/presentations.json` manifest instead of a TypeScript registry module.
Readiness is decided by capability probes (build script, resolvable `Presentation` export, parseable manifest) instead of anchor presence.
Puppeteer replaces Playwright as the browser-check dependency.
All templates are embedded in one `bootstrap.mjs`, run via the skill directory's absolute path, so no template lookup is needed.
A written plan naming the target and every file is shown and nothing is written before approval, instead of stating the target and confirming.
A CSS Module colocated with each presentation.
Every step at 1440×900 plus first, last, and two densest steps at 390×844, always rather than only for responsive-sensitive presentations.
`tsc --noEmit` followed by `vite build` instead of `npm run build`.
Automated bounding-box flags for canvas overflow and chrome intersections plus manual review.
Each warning's resolution is recorded in `review-log.md`; acceptance requires a written reason and `data-overlap-ok`.
The sample is linked from the landing page as the example.
The expected outline lives in `sample-outline.json` and is compared with the sample's step metadata.
Headless Chrome via Puppeteer against a Node static server over `dist/`, instead of Playwright against `vite preview`.
Captures wait for a runtime `data-settled="true"` signal instead of a configured settle interval.
Puppeteer and headless Chrome over the built bundle instead of Playwright/Chromium over `vite preview`.
Step count and current step are read from an ARIA `role="progressbar"` (`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuenow`) instead of `data-step-count`/`data-step-index`.
A generated bootstrap script with per-file content hashes checked by a unit test and the release check, instead of a manually synced snapshot.

unswapped_alternatives.reason: The Vite + React + TypeScript stack is fixed by the starting repository; only the build command changed (see INV-066).
Defined by the capabilities the runtime provides, which are kept.
Own folder, own route, one registration is intrinsic; the registration format changed under INV-044.
Behavior; delivered through the slot map (INV-013).
The project-local capture helper is the mechanism; only its command and output path changed.
The hybrid decision is the intent itself.
Renamed only (`npm run release-check`); still one documented entry point.
Primitives renamed (Node, Text, Connector, Enclosure, Highlight, Badge); same mechanism.

notes: Expected verdicts are all met, two more than the reference: the release-checks specification commits to stopping the server and browser after every run (INV-094, test-plan-only in the reference), and the template-parity hash check is a design decision (INV-118).
INV-075 is stated more firmly than in the reference: the sample is produced by running the skill, which exists first, and the brief and completion report are committed as evidence.

Only the normative sample values (title, chapter names, headlines, bodies, 880 × 380, "made by and-scene", 127.0.0.1) repeat reference text verbatim; no other sentence shares more than eight consecutive words with the reference.
Preference items are kept, so the input also serves as a fidelity-neutral baseline.
